name: Rockwood Museum
unique: A Gothic revival mansion with a conservatory, a carriage house and a park of specimen trees, built by a Quaker merchant family.
buzz: The house is unrestored in the best way and the grounds are free; the Christmas tours are the local tradition.

name: Old Swedes Church
unique: A Swedish Lutheran church built of local stone in 1698, one of the oldest churches in the country still in use, with a churchyard of colonial graves.
buzz: The stonework and the churchyard are the visit and the guides know the Swedish colonial history; it is quiet and free.

name: Brandywine Zoo
unique: A small zoo in Brandywine Park with a river otter, a bobcat and a farmyard, the kind of place you can finish before lunch.
buzz: Parents like the size and the shade and the park around it has a walking path along the Brandywine; it is cheap and never crowded.

name: Read House and Gardens
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A Federal mansion in the old colonial capital, with original wallpaper, a riverside garden and a collection of silver and furniture.
buzz: The house is the tour and the town of New Castle is the walk; the guides connect it to the state's colonial history.

name: John Dickinson Plantation
unique: The plantation of the man called the penman of the Revolution, with a Georgian house, outbuildings and the story of the enslaved people who worked the land.
buzz: The interpretation is honest about slavery and the house is furnished; it is free and quiet and the grounds are flat.

name: Legislative Hall
unique: A colonial revival capitol with a portrait gallery of every Delaware governor and a restored legislative chamber, free to tour.
buzz: The portraits and the chambers are the quick tour; the First State Heritage Park around it ties the town's history together.

name: First State Heritage Park
unique: A state park without land, a walking trail through Dover's colonial and state buildings including the old state house and the green.
buzz: The guided walks are the way to see inside the buildings and they run on weekends; the trail is flat and free.

name: Biggs Museum of American Art
customer: Art people, decorative arts fans, families
unique: A collection of Delaware valley furniture and silver from the 18th and 19th centuries, in a row of historic houses on the Dover green.
buzz: Furniture people call it a serious collection and it is free or nearly so; it is small and the period rooms are the charm.

name: Zwaanendael Museum
unique: A Dutch style building that looks like a town hall in Holland, holding the story of the 1631 Dutch settlement and the wreck of the DeBraak.
buzz: The building is the photograph and the shipwreck artifacts are the surprise; it is free and sits in the middle of Lewes.

name: Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Ten thousand acres of marsh and forest on Delaware Bay where eagles nest and the spring shorebird migration stops, with a driving loop.
buzz: The loop and the boardwalk are the easy way in and the refuge is quiet; the mosquitoes are serious in summer.

name: Lewes Historical Society Complex
customer: History people, families, house tour fans
unique: A campus of moved historic buildings including a 1730s plank house and a Coast Guard station, in the first town in the state.
buzz: The plank house is the oldest building in Delaware and the guides know it; the complex is small and the town walk is the rest.

name: Fenwick Island State Park
unique: A quiet barrier beach at the southern end of the state, between the ocean and Little Assawoman Bay, with a surf beach and a fishing area.
buzz: The beach is less crowded than Rehoboth and the bay side is calm; parking is the only cost and the state line is a short walk.

name: Chesapeake and Delaware Canal
unique: A 14 mile sea level canal across the Delmarva peninsula with a bike trail along the towpath and ships passing close enough to see the crew.
buzz: The ship watching is the reason to stop and the trail is flat; the canal is one of the busiest in the country.

name: Delaware Museum of Nature and Science
company: Delaware Museum of Nature and Science
unique: A natural history museum with a full dinosaur hall, a shell collection and live animals, in a park north of Wilmington.
buzz: The dinosaurs and the touch tanks are the family draws; it is small and the outdoor trails are free.

name: Ashland Nature Center
unique: A nature center in the Red Clay valley with trails through meadow and woods, a hawk watch and a stream for children to explore.
buzz: The hawk watch in fall is the local birding event and the trails are easy; it is quiet on weekdays.

name: Auburn Heights Preserve
unique: A mansion with a collection of Stanley steam cars and a one eighth scale steam railroad you can ride through the woods.
buzz: The steam train ride is the family draw and the cars are a surprise; it is run by volunteers and only open on weekends.

name: Delaware Agricultural Museum
unique: A museum of Delaware farming with a 1900s farmhouse, a barn of equipment and a chicken house, run by the state's agricultural community.
buzz: Children like the animals and the old kitchen and adults like the machinery; it is cheap and quiet.

name: Roger Williams Park Zoo
unique: A zoo in an Olmsted designed park with a rainforest building, elephants and a carousel, one of the oldest zoos in the country.
buzz: The rainforest and the elephants are the family stops and the park around it has a lake and a botanical center; it is big enough for a half day.

name: Providence Athenaeum
unique: A subscription library in a Greek revival building with a spiral staircase, gas lamps and the book club that Edgar Allan Poe reviewed for.
buzz: Book people call it one of the most beautiful rooms in New England and visitors are welcome to look; it is still a working library.

name: Sachuest Point National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A rocky peninsula between the Sakonnet and the Atlantic with trails along the shore, where harlequin ducks winter and monarchs stage in fall.
buzz: The winter waterfowl are the reason birders come and the loop trail is flat; the wind is constant and the paths are gravel.

name: International Yacht Restoration School
company: IYRS School of Technology and Trades
unique: A boatbuilding school on Newport harbor where you can watch students restore wooden yachts and a 1885 schooner in the water.
buzz: The workshop is open to visitors and the smell of varnish is the attraction; it is free and the students will explain what they are doing.

name: Ninigret National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A former naval airfield turned refuge of salt ponds and grassland where ospreys and herons nest and a bike path runs to the beach.
buzz: The trails and the salt pond are quiet and the bike path connects to the beach; the ticks are bad in summer.

name: East Greenwich Main Street
unique: A hilltop main street of 18th century houses and taverns ending at the harbor, with a view over Narragansett Bay from the bottom of the street.
buzz: Locals come for the restaurants and the water view and the street is small; the Hill and Harbour walk is the local after dinner route.

name: Vermont Historical Society Museum
unique: A state history museum next to the capitol with a gallery on the Green Mountain Boys, a 19th century kitchen and the state's original charter.
buzz: The charter and the Vermont identity exhibits are the reason to stop; it is free and small and pairs with the state house tour.

name: Ethan Allen Homestead
unique: The farm Ethan Allen built at the end of his life, with a rebuilt homestead and trails through the Winooski river valley.
buzz: The house and the Allen story are the visit and the trails are quiet; the site is small and the river walk is the bonus.

name: Vermont Institute of Natural Science
unique: A raptor center with bald eagles, hawks and owls in large flight enclosures, plus a forest canopy walk and a nature playscape.
buzz: The raptor enclosures are close enough to see feathers and the staff explain the injuries; the canopy walk is the family surprise.

name: Wilson Castle
customer: House tour people, photographers, curiosity seekers
unique: A brick and stone mansion with turrets, stained glass and a collection of Asian art, built by a English doctor in Vermont and never fully finished.
buzz: The house is strange and a little shabby and that is the charm; the guides tell the family story and the view over the valley is good.

name: Robert Frost Stone House Museum
unique: The stone house where Frost wrote Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening, with the orchard and the poem's landscape around it.
buzz: Poetry people come for the room where he wrote and the grounds are free; the museum is small and the docents know the poems.

name: Fairbanks Museum and Planetarium
unique: A Victorian natural history museum with a carved wooden ceiling, a weather station and a planetarium, founded by a scale manufacturer.
buzz: The hall of animals and the planetarium are the family stops and the building is the setting; it feels like 1890 in the best way.
